flagship.headline: Joni Mitchell sings Woodstock in public for the first time
flagship.summary_line_1: Joni Mitchell was not even on the bill, but she walked onto the stage at the Big Sur Folk Festival at the Esalen Institute and played her new song Woodstock in public for the first time, a performance her own archive dates to September 14.
flagship.summary_line_2: She had skipped the festival that inspired the song and built the lyric from Graham Nash's account of it, and within a year Woodstock had become a defining anthem of folk rock.

events.headline: Joni Mitchell sings Woodstock in public for the first time
events.summary_line_1: Joni Mitchell was not even on the bill, but she walked onto the stage at the Big Sur Folk Festival at the Esalen Institute and played her new song Woodstock in public for the first time, a performance her own archive dates to September 14.
events.summary_line_2: She had skipped the festival that inspired the song and built the lyric from Graham Nash's account of it, and within a year Woodstock had become a defining anthem of folk rock.

events.headline: The Jimi Hendrix Experience headline the Hollywood Bowl
events.summary_line_1: The Jimi Hendrix Experience headlined the Hollywood Bowl, with a water-filled moat set in front of the stage to keep fans from climbing up.
events.summary_line_2: The full set was recorded and later released on the 50th-anniversary edition of Electric Ladyland, catching the trio near its live peak in the middle of psychedelic rock.

events.headline: The Doors play two sets at Frankfurt's Kongresshalle
events.summary_line_1: The Doors played an early and a late show in one night at the Kongresshalle in Frankfurt on their first major European tour, with parts of both sets filmed for the German television show Beat-Club.
events.summary_line_2: The Frankfurt crowd, thick with American servicemen stationed nearby, saw Jim Morrison at his most theatrical months before the band's troubles deepened at home.

events.headline: A fire at Roy Orbison's home kills his two young sons
events.summary_line_1: A fire tore through Roy Orbison's house on Old Hickory Lake in Hendersonville, Tennessee, killing his sons Roy Jr. and Tony, aged 10 and 6, while their three-year-old brother Wesley was pulled to safety.
events.summary_line_2: Orbison was on a concert tour of England when the blaze broke out and chose to keep working, still closing shows with ballads like Crying.

events.headline: The Archie Show brings bubblegum pop to Saturday mornings
events.summary_line_1: The Archie Show premiered on CBS on a Saturday morning, an animated series built around the Archie comics with a studio band put together by Don Kirshner.
events.summary_line_2: Kirshner, fresh from the Monkees, used the cartoon to push bubblegum pop out of the Brill Building, and the house group topped the chart the next year with Sugar, Sugar.

events.headline: The Beatles film the tent scene for Magical Mystery Tour
events.summary_line_1: On the fourth day of filming Magical Mystery Tour, the Beatles shot the sequence of their coach passengers squeezing into a tiny tent, in a field near Newquay in Cornwall.
events.summary_line_2: In the finished film the tent opens onto the small theatre where George Harrison's Blue Jay Way sequence plays, and the crowds that gathered that day drew police to clear the traffic.

events.headline: George Harrison flies to Bombay to study sitar with Ravi Shankar
events.summary_line_1: George and Pattie Harrison landed in Bombay so George could study the sitar intensively with Ravi Shankar and take up yoga, hiding from Beatlemania at the Taj Mahal hotel under false names.
events.summary_line_2: He had just recorded Love You To, and the six weeks in India pushed Indian classical music further into the psychedelic sound of the late decade.

events.headline: Barbra Streisand records her first self-written melody
events.summary_line_1: Barbra Streisand returned to Columbia's New York studio to tape seven French and English numbers for Je m'appelle Barbra, among them Ma Premiere Chanson, the first tune she had written the melody for.
events.summary_line_2: The album, arranged largely by Michel Legrand, produced the single Free Again and moved her from Broadway belter toward international pop stylist.

events.headline: The Rolling Stones play Munich and Brian Jones meets Anita Pallenberg
events.summary_line_1: The Rolling Stones tore through two shows in one night at the Circus Krone in Munich on their first West German tour.
events.summary_line_2: Backstage between the sets, Brian Jones met the model and actress Anita Pallenberg, beginning a relationship that shaped the band's look and mood for years.

events.headline: Judy Garland finishes her last Greek Theatre show with a broken arm
events.summary_line_1: Judy Garland came back to the Greek Theatre for her second night with a broken arm, having tripped over her dog the day before, and got through only five songs.
events.summary_line_2: Mickey Rooney, Martha Raye and Johnny Mathis came onstage to carry her through, and the rest of the engagement was cancelled.

events.headline: The Beatles play their only Pittsburgh concert
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played their only Pittsburgh show, a quick afternoon house at the Civic Arena for 12,603 fans, then were driven straight back to the airport.
events.summary_line_2: The screaming buried the 12-song set, as it did everywhere on the 1964 North American tour.

events.headline: The Beach Boys' Surfer Girl reaches No. 7 on the Hot 100
events.summary_line_1: The Beach Boys' ballad Surfer Girl reached its peak of number seven on the Billboard Hot 100 dated September 14, 1963.
events.summary_line_2: It was the first record Brian Wilson produced on his own, a song he said he wrote in his car at nineteen.

events.headline: The Beatles headline Operation Big Beat V in New Brighton
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles topped a six-band, five-and-a-half-hour bill called Operation Big Beat V at the Tower Ballroom in New Brighton, Wallasey, promoted by Sam Leach.
events.summary_line_2: It was three weeks before Love Me Do reached the shops, with the band still a Merseyside draw rather than a national one at the front of the British Invasion.

events.headline: The Porter Wagoner Show premieres in syndication
events.summary_line_1: The Porter Wagoner Show began national syndication, a half-hour country variety program taped in Nashville and sponsored by a patent-medicine company.
events.summary_line_2: It ran until 1981 and gave classic country a weekly television home, later making a star of Dolly Parton after she joined the cast in 1967.

events.headline: Roosevelt Sykes cuts The Honeydripper at Van Gelder Studio
events.summary_line_1: The blues pianist Roosevelt Sykes recorded the album The Honeydripper at Rudy Van Gelder's studio in Englewood Cliffs, New Jersey, for Prestige's Bluesville label.
events.summary_line_2: The date teamed him with saxophonist King Curtis, whose own instrumental Soul Twist would top the R&B chart within two years.
